analysis.title: L'Oreal: Model update
key_insights: RBC raises its adjusted present value price target on L'Oréal to €480 from €450 and retains an Outperform rating after the 3Q 2026 results.

The analyst says L'Oréal has delivered the best consistent volume growth in RBC's consumer staples universe for many years and expects that to continue. Volume growth is described as the best indicator of share price performance.
EBITA estimates rise to €9.6bn for 2026E (prev. €9.5bn), €10.6bn for 2027E (prev. €10.3bn) and €11.5bn for 2028E (prev. €11.2bn).
Ops diluted EPS estimates rise to €13.44 for 2026E (prev. €13.32), €14.75 for 2027E (prev. €14.36) and €15.93 for 2028E (prev. €15.52).
The APV gives a fair value of €455 per share at a 7.0% cost of equity and 2.5% perpetuity growth. Discounting forward a year and deducting the forecast dividend gives the €480 12-month target.

Scenario values are €590 upside (+39%) and €370 downside (-12%) against a €430.10 price. The upside case assumes sales growth 1 point above base and EBIT margin 100bps above base. The downside case assumes sales growth 200bps below base and EBIT margin 200bps below base.

The report acknowledges that L'Oréal's recent performance came in below expectations amid a challenging macro backdrop. RBC sees this as temporary and says the de-rating over the last year suggests the risk is to the upside.
Beauty is described as a hiding place from the risk of lower Gen Z consumption seen in tobacco and beverages.

RBC forecasts 2026E organic growth of 6.9%, reported sales growth of 8.9%, and EBIT margin after restructuring of 20.0%. The 2026E forecast includes €8.27bn of M&A outflow, which lifts net debt to €7.5bn.
On valuation, L'Oréal trades at 31.8x 2026E and 29.0x 2027E P/E, against a Food and HPC average of 19.8x and 18.6x and an HPC average of 24.9x and 22.2x.

market_movers.rationale: The target rises to €480 from €450 after the 3Q 2026 results and higher forecasts. Rating retained on best-in-universe volume growth.

sector_views.rationale: RBC calls the beauty category well positioned on structural demographic shifts and ongoing innovation. It also sees beauty as insulated from the lower Gen Z consumption risk affecting tobacco and beverages.
The report cites lower Gen Z consumption as a real long-term concern in tobacco and beverages. BAT is rated Underperform with a €... target of £38 against a £45 share price.

earnings_insights: L'Oréal 3Q 2026 results are described as having come in below expectations, which RBC views as temporary. The report gives no reported 3Q figures.
RBC 2026E ops diluted EPS is €13.44 (RBC estimate, prev. €13.32), against 2025A of €12.43 (reported, after restructuring). Adjusted EPS is €13.71 for 2026E (estimate) and €12.72 for 2025A.
RBC estimates for 2026E: revenue €48.0bn, EBITA €9.6bn, organic growth 6.9% and reported growth 8.9%. All are forecasts, not reported figures.
2026E estimated EBIT margin after restructuring is 20.0%, with underlying EBIT margin of 20.4%. The underlying margin change is 32bps (RBC estimate).
DPS is forecast at €7.79 for 2026E (prev. €7.72) and €8.55 for 2027E (prev. €8.32), against 2025A of €7.20.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A model input for the terminal value, not a macro forecast.
The discount rate applied to operating cash flows in the valuation.

trade_ideas.description: Outperform rating on L'Oréal (NXT PA: OR) with a 12-month price target of €480 against a €430.10 price
trade_ideas.rationale: Best consistent volume growth in RBC's consumer staples universe, a de-rated valuation and a growth recovery that could surprise on the upside.
trade_ideas.risk: Weaker consumer confidence in China, price competition in Consumer Products, Aesop underperformance, unsuccessful innovation and injectables reducing beauty consumption.

risk_factors: Further deterioration in consumer confidence in key markets, particularly China, would hurt sales and margins.
More intense price competition, especially in Consumer Products, could weigh on top-line growth. Effective competitor innovation could further slow Dermatological Beauty.
Worse-than-expected performance of the recent major acquisition, Aesop, would be negative for the shares.
Unsuccessful innovation could weaken L'Oréal's market positioning and share gains.
Higher adoption of injectables could lower consumption of beauty products.

tension_points.bull_case: RBC sees the recent shortfall as temporary, the pace of recovery as able to surprise on the upside, and the de-rating over the last year as leaving risk skewed up. Volume growth is the best in its staples universe.
tension_points.bear_case: Recent performance came in below expectations amid a challenging macro backdrop. Consumer confidence in China could weaken further, and price competition and injectables adoption could cut beauty consumption.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further deterioration in consumer confidence in key markets, particularly China, which RBC says would hurt sales and margins.
